correctness.rationale: The clumsy empty/singleton loss-set law and the independent-Bernoulli deletion law overlap only on zero- and one-element sets, giving exact TV delta=epsilon[1-(1-p)^(n-1)]<=c²/n². Independently verified the identity by exact rational enumeration for n=3,5,7. With common acquisition proposals, B_t⊆V_t for clumsy B and always-acquire V; each gap originates at a loss round with a missing proposed coupon and is cleared by its next successful acquisition. A one-coupon absent marginal u_s=epsilon+(1-epsilon)(1-1/n)^s bounds active gaps. Union bounds and no early completion among classical proposals yield the displayed finite error for times h=floor(n log n/2), H=ceil(n log n+Kn), O(log n/sqrt n). Use previously proved clumsy Theorem 4.10 to transfer weak convergence to G+tau_c. The theorem is about labelled sets and post-update hitting times, not just means.

value.rationale: The two naturally studied nonmonotone coupon processes have equal expected total deletion intensity but distinct updates; that alone does not ensure agreement of rare completion times. The explicit pathwise high-probability comparison provides a robust universality bridge between independent multi-loss events and one-label-refresh, with a finite error certificate across the entire critical window. The source clumsy limit is correctly credited and the new implication matters independently.

final_claim: Critical p=c/n² post-loss careless process couples pathwise to clumsy epsilon=c/n across completion window with O_c,K(log n/sqrt n) failure, transferring known G+tau_c law.
limitations: Critical clumsy limit is cited, not certified anew; general perturbation/coupling priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: Only fixed c>0, uniform proposals, post-update completion, and window compact K; no convergence of moments or all-time coupling.
Published clumsy limit treated as external theorem, not independently re-proved.
